The best way is to just read the news for 30 minutes a day. There are a couple of caveats, though:

  • Limit yourself to elite media: I personally love the Economist and Foreign Policy; read the NYT/WSJ (or similar papers) for daily news. Try to avoid online sources (like HuffPo) and cable news, at least at first..

  • Get your news from a wide variety of sources. Don't just find articles on voat/reddit - or, if you do, be sure to actively seek out articles from sources on the other side. If you see a NYT article on something, try to read the WSJ article on it. If you see a Fox News article, look for the MSNBC article on it.

  • Remember that journalists often miss important nuance. If you hear something that just sounds crazy (e.g. "Supreme court rules that corporations are literally people!"), you're probably not being shown the nuance.

I think it's important to get your news from multiple sources. Anyone who gets all their information from just Fox News or the Huffington Post or some talking head on TV will only be getting part of the story. Inform yourself of positions you disagree with and don't just become another member in the giant cirlclejerk of a political party. The truth is, very few people align 100% with any party.
